newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse sees uncertain near-future.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse sees uncertain near-future.

text.p: Belgian shares which ended higher on Wednesday, ignoring fears of further U.S. interest rate hikes, were expected to settle down in coming days as U.S. interest rate hike fears gathered pace, traders said.
The Brussels Bel-20 index closed up 0.87 percent at 2,124.40 points, with a firm 3.4 billion francs volume of Belgian shares traded.
"With the U.S. February durable goods data out -- stronger than expected -- I'm worried the Fed will push up rates in May," said one trader.
Dealers said Belgian shares would be hard hit if the U.S. economy showed further signs of overheating.
But one trader said the Belgian market would benefit from the firm dollar, which could hold gains despite U.S. rate hikes.
"Dollar sensitive stocks are the ones you want to hold on to," said another trader.
Another trader said a strong dollar was not enough to keep up stocks because Wall Street set the direction for the Brussels bourse.
Attention was on electronics group Barco with investors piling into the share expecting strong 1996 earnings.
The share closed 1.81 percent higher at 5,620 francs.
Barco announced after bourse close that 1996 current profit was up 31 percent.
"Barco can hold at these levels," said another trader.
Elsewhere Groupe Lambert Bruxelles (GBL) closed up 2.4 percent at 4,910 francs, after it posted 16.6 percent increase in 1996 net current profit.
Retailer Colruyt jumped 2.51 percent to 14,300 francs, with dealers putting it down to a recovery from recent profit-taking.
Cement marker CBR closed up 1.67 percent at 3,345 francs, helped by a firm dollar and a recovery from profit-taking.
